Keep such a candidate exploratory unless candidate-specific evidence supports acceptance of the limiting partner. Prioritize the feasibility of the target-specific transformation and substrate acceptance over a generic mechanism match. Different distributions or counts of functional groups can supply equivalent complementary reacting ends. Whole-molecule overlap is supporting context, never a requirement or a reason by itself to reject such a route. Native annotation, an enzyme class, a shared bond label, a high similarity score, or merely using an energy cofactor cannot establish relevance. Identify the actual activated center and reacting partners; distinguish donors, carriers, auxiliary substrates and direct nucleophiles. Check local reacting atoms and bond-order changes rather than relying on EC labels or matching functional groups elsewhere in a molecule. Algorithmic classifications are fallible interpretations; prefer reaction equations and structures. Explain candidate-specific catalytic machinery, target partner roles, adaptations and constraints. A different native substrate does not alone imply inactivity. Missing native annotation does not exclude a candidate if independent mechanistic evidence supports a testable hypothesis. Defer when no defensible target-specific hypothesis can be formed; exclude only on observed incompatibility. Structural activation geometry is separate from the complete requested reaction and is not an activity measurement. Do not invent numerical geometry thresholds or apply a criterion to a different reacting center. Use only the declared site criteria. Prioritize defensible starting points for this target. The requested reaction may have no documented activity for any enzyme; that absence is the premise of the work and is not by itself a reason to withhold priority. Judge a candidate on its own mechanistic case and on evidence that substrate recognition could transfer, such as relevant promiscuity, native scaffold tolerance, or native partners resembling the requested ones. Investigate denotes a weaker or unresolved hypothesis. Decide on absolute evidence, not which candidate is best within this batch. Zero prioritized candidates is a valid result. Matching native reacting atom classes alone is insufficient for priority: explain candidate-specific evidence supporting transfer of substrate recognition, such as relevant promiscuity, native scaffold tolerance or architecture. Use one record_target_assessment call per candidate. source_refs must contain exactly its supplied R-indexed source ID, without additional citations. Map every T-indexed target participant, including any nonreacting spectator. Preserve unknowns and state a discriminating reopening condition. Distinguish measured native activity for this exact protein from automatically inferred annotation and experiments on a related protein. Distinguish detectable substrate turnover from efficient turnover. Inspect quantitative relative activity, kinetics, conditions and controls in primary sources when available; a substrate being listed in a database does not establish that it is a good substrate. A database reaction annotation, reviewed status, or literature hit count does not alone establish experimental characterization. For prioritize or investigate, evidence_level must be direct_target_observation or mechanistic_transfer and strengths must contain candidate-specific support. Otherwise defer; never upgrade the evidence level just to satisfy validation. Keep each assessment around 200–250 words total, using concise source-specific findings. Avoid repeating the target description or generic caveats in multiple fields. Do not invent evidence, experiments, identities or missing native substrates.

Investigate denotes a weaker or unresolved hypothesis. Decide on absolute evidence, not which candidate is best within this batch. Zero prioritized candidates is a valid result. Map every T-indexed target participant, including any nonreacting spectator. Preserve unknowns and state a discriminating reopening condition. Distinguish detectable substrate turnover from efficient turnover. Inspect quantitative relative activity, kinetics, conditions and controls in primary sources when available; a substrate being listed in a database does not establish that it is a good substrate. A database reaction annotation, reviewed status, or literature hit count does not alone establish experimental characterization. Otherwise defer; never upgrade the evidence level just to satisfy validation. Keep each assessment around 200–250 words total, using concise source-specific findings. Avoid repeating the target description or generic caveats in multiple fields. Do not invent evidence, experiments, identities or missing native substrates.
